newsitem.title: USA: Onyx says test patients tolerate ONYX-015.
newsitem.headline: Onyx says test patients tolerate ONYX-015.

text.p: Onyx Pharmaceuticals Inc said Tuesday that patients participating in a trial of ONYX-015 tolerated the adenovirus, which has been genetically engineered to fight tumor cells.
"Treatment with ONYX-015 was well-tolerated by all of the 32 patients completing the trial," it said in a statement.

Onyx said preclinical trials had shown that the adenovirus "efficiently" replicated in and killed tumor cells deficient in p53 tumor suppressor gene activity. Mutations in p53 are the most common type of genetic abnormality in cancer, occurring in more than 50 percent of human cancer cases, it added.

The company said six of 19 patients receiving a single injection of ONYX-015 experienced "significant" necrosis of the injected tumor masses. In comparison, six of nine patients treated with the virus daily for five days experienced necrosis ranging from 30 to 90 percent of their tumor mass, it said.
"In addition, tumor necrosis was associated with clinical benefit in some of the patients, including decreased pain, improved ability to swallow and improved speech," it added.

The 30 patients participating in the trial will initially receive injections of ONYX-015 directly into a target tumor and then into additional tumors, if present, after the second cycle of treatment, it said.
ONYX said it was conducting the Phase II trials at 12 sites in the United States, United Kingdom and Canada.
